model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-Fos + Alexa Fluor 488, NeuN + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent fluorescence preservation and compatibility with lipid removal using organic solvents. It allows deep imaging of fluorescent signals in large tissue volumes, which is essential for mapping activated neurons (e.g., C-Fos) at single-cell resolution across the entire brain. The combination of C-Fos (an immediate early gene marker of neuronal activation) and NeuN (a pan-neuronal marker) enables precise identification and spatial localization of activated neurons within different brain regions. Alexa Fluor dyes are highly photostable and compatible with iDISCO+.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Lipid Removal (Delipidation)  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining (Labeling)  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail:  
  – Anti-C-Fos (1:500 dilution in blocking solution)  
  – Anti-NeuN (1:500 dilution in blocking solution)  
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail:  
  – Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500)  
  – Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500)  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Repeat step 4.4 (Wash) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Final Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

6 Delipidation (Second Round)  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in a custom chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-Fos + Alexa Fluor 488 antibody, Npas4 + Alexa Fluor 594 antibody]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole mouse brain clearing with strong fluorescence preservation and delipidation efficiency. It allows deep imaging of fluorescent signals in intact brains, which is essential for mapping activated neurons at single-cell resolution across the entire brain. The methanol-based protocol is compatible with lipid-soluble dyes and secondary antibodies used for IEG labeling (e.g., C-Fos and Npas4). This method also provides more uniform clearing than simplified CUBIC protocols, especially for large tissue volumes like adult mouse brains.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (DMSO/Triton solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2 Replace DMSO/Triton solution every 24 hours to maintain reagent activity

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4 Immunostaining (Optional if endogenous IEGs are not sufficient or need amplification)  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies:  
  – Anti-C-Fos (1:500 dilution)  
  – Anti-Npas4 (1:500 dilution)  
  in PBS with 2% normal goat serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies:  
  – Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-species IgG (1:500)  
  – Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-species IgG (1:500)  
  in PBS with 2% normal goat serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour for washing)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution: 60% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE), 30% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 10% (vol/vol) 2,2-thiodiethanol (TDE) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with final clearing solution: 100% DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in DBE for light-sheet microscopy or confocal imaging  
6.2 Store cleared brain in DBE at 4 ℃ until imaging

This dual labeling strategy allows for the visualization of both axonal tracts and their myelination status, which is essential for analyzing regeneration and connectivity.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Lipid Removal (Delipidation)  
2.1 Incubation with 100% methanol + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% methanol + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% methanol + 30% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% methanol + 50% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol + 100% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Clearing Agent Exchange  
3.1 Incubation with 100% DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Sigma-Aldrich, D1416) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% DBE containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

5 Labeling (Pre-clearing)  
5.1 Incubation with DiI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for intracellular labeling of axons (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with anti-Olig2 primary antibody (1:500 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.6 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

6 Final Clearing and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Optional: Add 0.1% (vol/vol) Hoechst 33342 to DBE for nuclear counterstaining (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Wash briefly with fresh DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)

7.1 Store sample in 100% DBE at 4 ℃ until imaging  
7.2 For light-sheet microscopy, transfer sample into a custom chamber filled with DBE and cover with a glass slide for imaging

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for lipid removal in thick nervous tissue such as spinal cord, and it preserves fluorescent signals effectively, especially from robust fluorophores like mCherry and lipophilic dyes like DiI. The methanol-based delipidation allows deep penetration of light for 3D imaging. mCherry can label mature or residual axons via transgenic expression or viral tracing, while DiI labels regenerating or newly formed fibers due to its passive diffusion along myelinated axons. This dual labeling strategy enables simultaneous visualization of both mature and regenerating axonal structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Lipid Removal (Delipidation)  
2.1 Incubation with 100% methanol + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% methanol + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% methanol + 30% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% methanol + 50% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Clearing Agent Exchange  
3.1 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Sigma-Aldrich, D1416) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with fresh DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% DBE (final clearing solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

5 Imaging Preparation (Optional RI Adjustment)  
5.1 For light-sheet microscopy, incubate in 100% DBE with 0.1% (w/v) Pluronic F-127 (optional for improved optical homogeneity) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Fluorescent Labeling (Prior to Clearing)  
6.1 Apply DiI (1–5 μg/μL in ethanol) directly onto the surface of the spinal cord at the injury site using a fine-tipped applicator (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubate sample in PBS at 37 °C for 24–48 hours to allow DiI diffusion along axons  
6.3 Wash 3× with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 min each) to remove unbound dye

7 Post-Clearing Storage  
7.1 Store cleared samples in 100% DBE at 4 °C in the dark until imaging

**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based optical clearing method that preserves tissue integrity and fluorescence signals effectively, making it ideal for long-term preservation of delicate structures such as axons in spinal cord injury models. It avoids the use of harsh organic solvents or electric fields, which minimizes tissue fragmentation during delipidation—critical for maintaining spatial continuity across the injury epicenter and adjacent regions. DiI is an excellent lipophilic tracer for labeling and tracking long-distance axonal pathways, while GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) labeled with Alexa Fluor 488 provides a robust marker for reactive astrocytes and glial scar formation, enabling co-registration of structural and cellular changes.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-R0) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-R1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-R2) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-R4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS containing 5% (wt/vol) SDS (CUBIC-D1) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS containing 5% (wt/vol) SDS and 25% (vol/vol) iohexol (CUBIC-C1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole CNS clearing due to its strong delipidation capability and compatibility with fluorescent proteins such as GFP and tdTomato. It allows deep imaging of long-range projections in large tissue volumes (up to 40 mm), which is essential for tracing cortical projections through the brainstem into the spinal cord. The use of transgenic or viral-based dual-color labeling (e.g., Cre-dependent AAVs or reporter lines) enables specific and distinct visualization of two independent fiber populations or pathways, facilitating analysis of their spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Optional Permeabilization and Antibody Staining (if required)  
4.1 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum in 0.1% Triton X-100/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with primary antibody (e.g., anti-GFAP, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit, 1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3

5 Final Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

6 Final Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% dibenzyl ether, DBE; Sigma-Aldrich, D1419) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with DBE (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in DBE within a custom-made chamber or glass-bottom dish for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal imaging.  
8.2 Ensure sample is fully submerged and free from air bubbles.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, DiI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based optical clearing method that preserves endogenous and exogenous fluorescent signals effectively, making it ideal for long-term 3D imaging of large CNS samples (up to several centimeters in length). It is compatible with GFP and lipophilic dyes like DiI, which are essential for visualizing both genetically labeled long-range projections and overall axonal architecture. The aqueous nature of CUBIC avoids delipidation-induced signal loss, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of lipid-soluble markers such as DiI. This makes CUBIC particularly suitable for tracing continuous fiber pathways from cortex to spinal cord.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 24 hours at 4 °C to permeabilize tissue. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash 3 times with PBS for 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Primary Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with anti-GFP antibody (1:500 dilution in PBS + 0.1% BSA) for 72 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)
2.2 Wash 3 times with PBS for 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 dilution in PBS + 0.1% BSA) for 48 hours at 4 °C. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Wash 3 times with PBS for 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with DiI (1:1000 dilution in DMSO/PBS) for 72 hours at 4 °C to label whole axonal network. (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)
2.6 Wash 3 times with PBS for 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) CUBIC reagent (CUBIC-R; 40% w/v urea, 25% w/v glucose, 25% w/v fructose in PBS) for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 20% CUBIC-R for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 30% CUBIC-R for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 40% CUBIC-R for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.5 Incubation with 50% CUBIC-R for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R for 72 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-C (100% CUBIC-R + 10% wt/vol PEG400) for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.2 Incubation with CUBIC-C (100% CUBIC-R + 20% wt/vol PEG400) for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
5.3 Incubation with CUBIC-C (100% CUBIC-R + 30% wt/vol PEG400) for 24 hours at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation
6.1 Mount sample in CUBIC-C solution for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: As needed for imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry, DiI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole CNS clearing due to its lipid-removal-based approach, which effectively clears large tissue volumes (up to 35–40 mm) while preserving fluorescent signals such as mCherry and lipophilic dyes like DiI. It allows long-range imaging of neural tracts in intact tissues using light-sheet microscopy. The combination of mCherry (for transsynaptic or viral tracing) and DiI (for anterograde/retrograde labeling of axons) provides dual fluorescence that can distinguish target projection fibers from the endogenous white matter network. This strategy supports 3D reconstruction of long-range pathways from cortex to spinal cord.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% methanol + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Replace DMSO with 100% DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Repeat step 2.3 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% DBE (Diethyl Sebacate) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 75% DBE in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% DBE in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 25% DBE in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with 0% DBE (PBS only) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4 Fluorescence Staining (Optional Secondary Markers)  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody solution (e.g., anti-Olig2, 1:500 in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days)  
4.4 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (100% DBE) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in custom chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet microscopy (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: As needed for imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves fluorescence and tissue morphology well, making it ideal for long-term imaging of large CNS samples (35–40 mm). It avoids the severe shrinkage and fluorescence quenching associated with organic solvent-based methods like iDISCO+. The use of endogenous GFP and tdTomato allows for high signal retention and specificity for long-range axonal tracing. CUBIC also supports RI matching for light-sheet microscopy, which is essential for 3D imaging of deep structures such as brainstem and spinal cord.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-R0) at 4 ℃ for 24 hours.  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS at 4 ℃ for 24 hours.  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS at 4 ℃ for 24 hours.  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS at 4 ℃ for 24 hours.  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS at 4 ℃ for 48 hours.  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (100% ethylene glycol + 2.5% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS) at 37 ℃ for 72 hours.  
2.2 Replace CUBIC-R1 every 24 hours to maintain delipidation efficiency.  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (100% ethylene glycol + 2.5% (wt/vol) SDS + 25% (wt/vol) glucose in PBS) at 37 ℃ for 72 hours.  
3.2 Replace CUBIC-R2 every 24 hours.  

4 Final Clearing and Stabilization  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R3 (100% ethylene glycol + 2.5% (wt/vol) SDS + 50% (wt/vol) glucose in PBS) at 37 ℃ for 72 hours.  
4.2 Replace CUBIC-R3 every 24 hours.  

5 Post-Clearing Washing and Fluorescence Enhancement  
5.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 24 hours at RT to remove residual detergent and stabilize fluorescence.  
5.2 Wash 3× with PBS for 1 hour each at RT.  

6 Refractive Index Matching for Imaging  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-F (final refractive index-matched solution: 100% ethylene glycol + 2.5% (wt/vol) SDS + 50% (wt/vol) glucose in PBS) at 37 ℃ for 24 hours.  
6.2 Store sample in CUBIC-F at 4 ℃ until imaging.  

7 Imaging Preparation (Optional)  
7.1 For light-sheet microscopy, transfer sample into a custom chamber filled with CUBIC-F or a compatible immersion medium (e.g., GLOX, RI ~1.49).  
7.2 Mount sample on a rotating stage or in agarose block if necessary for stable imaging.

**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 488, Congo Red]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole-brain clearing of fixed mouse brains and provides excellent compatibility with lipid removal and refractive index matching using dibenzyl ether (DBE). It preserves fluorescent signals effectively, especially when combined with robust primary antibodies and chromogenic or small-molecule dyes. The combination of a specific Aβ antibody (6E10) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 and Congo Red—a classical amyloid-specific dye—provides two independent but complementary labeling strategies for Aβ plaques. This dual approach enhances detection sensitivity and enables validation of plaque morphology and distribution in deep brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with 6E10 antibody (1:500 dilution in iDISCO+ blocking solution: 10% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in DBE) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)

4 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in iDISCO+ blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 2 hours)

5 Congo Red Staining  
5.1 Incubation with 0.05% (wt/vol) Congo Red in 80% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Washing with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Washing with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Rehydration through 80%, 50%, and 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (each step: Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.5 Final wash in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Sigma-Aldrich, D1398) without shaking (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Optional additional incubation in DBE for up to 48 hours for improved optical clarity

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store sample in fresh DBE at 4 °C until imaging

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 + Alexa Fluor 594, GFAP + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for lipid removal in brain tissue and provides excellent optical clearing while preserving fluorescent signals from antibodies. It is compatible with standard immunostaining protocols and allows deep imaging of vascular networks (CD31) and astrocytic structures (GFAP), which are essential for analyzing tumor-vascular interactions in GBM. The methanol-based delipidation ensures compatibility with hydrophobic clearing agents like dibenzyl ether (DBE). This method supports high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging of the 3D tumor-vascular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Lipid Removal  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail:  
  – CD31 (1:200, e.g., BD Pharmingen #553370)  
  – GFAP (1:500, e.g., Agilent Z0334)  
 in 5% NGS/0.3% Triton X-100/PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail:  
  – Anti-rat IgG (Alexa Fluor 594, 1:500, e.g., Thermo A-21207)  
  – Anti-mouse IgG (Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500, e.g., Thermo A-11001)  
 in 5% NGS/0.3% Triton X-100/PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times

5 Re-dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014-1KG) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Replace DBE and incubate again (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in DBE within a custom chamber or glass-bottom dish for imaging  
8.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal microscopy

我尝试使用 CUBIC 处理 GBM 脑组织，但透明化后肿瘤组织形态破坏严重，血管网络出现断裂，导致无法可靠分析肿瘤边界、血管连续性和沿血管侵袭路径。原 protocol 为：CUBIC-L 在 37°C 处理 7 天，然后直接放入 CUBIC-R。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法，使其适合肿瘤脑组织形态保持、血管网络连续性保留、屏障相关结构检测和深层三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5 + Alexa Fluor 488, mCherry (tumor reporter), IB4 (pericyte marker)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol-based delipidation method that preserves fluorescence and structural integrity of complex tissues like brain with tumor infiltration. It allows for deep imaging in large tissue blocks while maintaining vascular network continuity and BBB-related structures such as Claudin-5 and pericytes (IB4). Compared to CUBIC, it avoids excessive swelling and distortion, which are likely responsible for the observed morphological disruption. The labeling strategy combines CD31 for endothelial cells, Claudin-5 for tight junctions, mCherry for tumor visualization, and IB4 for pericyte coverage—enabling comprehensive analysis of vascular architecture and tumor-vascular interactions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (iDISCO-D) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Refractive Index Matching (RI-Raise)  
3.1 Incubation with RI-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with RI-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with RI-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI = 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Final Clearing Agent Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO-R (100% dibenzyl ether, DBE) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

5 Post-Clearing Washing and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 1 hour at RT to remove residual detergent  
5.2 Incubate with PBS containing 0.1% BSA and 0.01% NaN₃ for 1 hour at RT to stabilize fluorescent signals

6 Imaging Setup  
6.1 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with iDISCO-R or RI-matched oil (e.g., Immersol 514F)  
6.2 Perform light-sheet or confocal microscopy using appropriate excitation/emission filters for mCherry, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence well, making it ideal for weak signals such as sparse GFP-labeled neurons. It is gentle on tissue and compatible with long-term storage in CUBIC-R solution. The combination of endogenous GFP and exogenous MAP2 staining (to highlight dendritic structures) provides dual labeling to visualize both neuronal somata and dendritic morphology in 3D. This strategy supports detailed morphological analysis while minimizing photobleaching and signal loss.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-U (50 mM NaCl, 100 mM choline chloride, 0.5% wt/vol TX-100, 0.2% wt/vol BSA in PBS) (Temperature: 37 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Replace CUBIC-U every 24 hours; repeat incubation for total 72 hours

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R (50 mM NaCl, 100 mM choline chloride, 0.2% wt/vol BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Post-Clearing Staining (Optional Enhancement)  
5.1 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 1% BSA in PBS for blocking (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (1:500 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-IgG (1:1000 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS for washing (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

6 Final Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R (50 mM NaCl, 100 mM choline chloride, 0.2% wt/vol BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Long-Term Storage / Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store in CUBIC-R at 4 °C for long-term preservation or proceed to imaging  
7.2 For light-sheet microscopy, ensure RI matching by confirming no bubbles or phase mismatch in the sample before imaging

This combination ensures minimal signal loss over 6 months and compatibility with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC reagent A (urea 10%, SDS 0.5%) in 30% glycerol/PBS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC reagent A (urea 10%, SDS 0.5%) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC reagent B (urea 10%, SDS 0.5%, 50% glycerol) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with CUBIC reagent C (urea 10%, SDS 0.5%, 80% glycerol) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC reagent D (urea 10%, SDS 0.5%, 100% glycerol) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4.1 Permeabilization with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5 Final Washing and Storage Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Store in CUBIC reagent D at 4 ℃ for long-term preservation (up to 6 months)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence well and is compatible with long-term storage in CUBIC-R solution. It is particularly suitable for weak fluorescent signals such as those from sparse reporter mice, and it allows for repeated imaging over time without significant signal degradation. The use of dual-color transgenic reporters (e.g., GFP and tdTomato) enables simultaneous visualization of multiple neuronal populations or structures, which is essential for analyzing dendritic complexity and local circuitry.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-D1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-D2) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-D3) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (CUBIC-D4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Lipid Removal  
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol + 5% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS (CUBIC-L1) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol + 10% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS (CUBIC-L2) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol + 15% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS (CUBIC-L3) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R (80% ethylene glycol + 20% triethylene glycol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Fluorescence Stabilization (Optional but recommended for long-term preservation)  
4.1 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) PFA in CUBIC-R (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Wash with CUBIC-R three times, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

5 Storage / Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Store samples in fresh CUBIC-R at 4 ℃ for up to 6 months  
5.2 For imaging, transfer samples to CUBIC-R and mount on a glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R for light-sheet or confocal microscopy

6 Optional Post-Storage Re-imaging Protocol  
6.1 After 6 months, re-incubate in CUBIC-R for 24 hours at RT to restore optical clarity if needed  
6.2 Perform additional washes in CUBIC-R if fluorescence intensity has decreased slightly  
6.3 Proceed with imaging using the same mounting conditions

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for lipid-rich and dense tissues such as human brain cortex due to its delipidation-based clearing mechanism. It preserves fluorescent signals effectively, especially when using robust secondary antibodies and lipophilic dyes. The dual labeling strategy with NeuN (a mature neuron marker) and IB4 (which labels unmyelinated axons and microglia) allows for the visualization of both neuronal somata and associated structures, enabling accurate 3D mapping of mature neurons across cortical layers. Alexa Fluor conjugates are photostable and compatible with iDISCO+.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% methanol/DCM (1:2 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Repeat step 2.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol/DCM (2:1 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody mix:  
 - Mouse anti-NeuN (1:500 dilution)  
 - Biotinylated IB4 lectin (1:200 dilution)  
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody mix:  
 - Anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution)  
 - Streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500 dilution)  
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.4 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

5 Final Dehydration and Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol/DCM (1:2 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.7 Repeat step 5.6 (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% methanol/DCM (2:1 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 50% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with RI matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with RI matching solution (80% glycerol in PBS)  
7.2 Allow equilibration at RT for at least 2 hours before imaging  
7.3 Proceed with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D reconstruction

**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves fluorescence and allows deep antibody penetration in thick brain tissue, making it ideal for 3 mm human cortical slices. It avoids harsh organic solvents, which can quench fluorescent signals. The combination of NeuN (a mature neuron marker) with Alexa Fluor 488 and DAPI provides dual labeling for nuclear and neuronal cell body detection, enabling accurate 3D localization and density analysis. This strategy ensures compatibility with CUBIC’s aqueous environment and supports long-term imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)

3 Antigen Retrieval (Optional but recommended for thick human tissue)  
3.1 Incubation with 10 mM sodium citrate buffer (pH 6.0), heated to 95 °C in microwave (Temperature: 95 °C, Time: 10 minutes)  
3.2 Cool down to RT in the same buffer (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4 Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN primary antibody (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-Clear solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)  
4.2 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in CUBIC-Clear solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-Clear solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 days)

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-Wash solution (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 3 × 24 hours)

7 Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-Clear solution (10% (w/v) urea, 25% (v/v) glycerol, 25% (v/v) tetraethylene glycol monododecyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 7 days)

8 RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-RiM solution (50% (v/v) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with CUBIC-RiM solution (75% (v/v) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with CUBIC-RiM solution (100% (v/v) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)

9 Storage and Imaging  
9.1 Store sample in CUBIC-RiM solution at 4 °C until imaging  
9.2 Mount in CUBIC-RiM or similar high-RI medium for light-sheet or confocal imaging

实验室新人进行厚人脑皮层神经元染色时出现问题：染色后只有表层约 1 mm 有信号，深层组织完全无标记。实验记录显示：固定用了 24 h；荧光标记试剂在 4°C 孵育 72 h；用 PBS 稀释荧光标记试剂。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法，使其适合厚人脑皮层组织的充分固定、抗体深层渗透、成熟神经元双信号检测、透明化和三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves fluorescence and allows deep antibody penetration in thick brain tissue, making it ideal for 3 mm human cortical slices. It avoids harsh organic solvents, which can quench fluorescent signals. The combination of NeuN (a mature neuron marker) with Alexa Fluor 488 and DAPI provides dual labeling for nuclear and neuronal cell body detection, enabling accurate 3D localization, cell counting, and laminar analysis. This strategy ensures compatibility with CUBIC’s aqueous environment and supports high-resolution imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-NeuN (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-C solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with DAPI (1:10,000 dilution in CUBIC-C solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

4 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-C solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

5 Wash  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-C solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Repeat step 5.1 two more times

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R solution (CUBIC reagent, 80% urea, 20% iohexol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R solution for light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a fast and effective lipid-clearing method suitable for fixed thick brain slices (500 μm), with excellent compatibility with fluorescent proteins like GFP and mCherry. This combination supports high-resolution imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Fluorescent Staining (Optional Enhancement)  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated Phalloidin (1:100 dilution in PBS) to label F-Actin (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Wash 3× with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min each)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution: 80% dibenzyl ether (DBE) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Sigma-Aldrich, 108014-1KG) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount samples in 100% DBE in a custom chamber or glass-bottom dish for light-sheet or confocal imaging

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, MAP2+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence well and is particularly suitable for thin to medium thickness brain slices (e.g., 500 μm). It allows rapid clearing within 1 day and is compatible with high-resolution imaging of fine structures such as dendritic spines and dendritic arbors. The labeling strategy combines an endogenously expressed fluorescent reporter (GFP) for sparse neuronal labeling and a post-fixed immunostaining marker (MAP2) labeled with Alexa Fluor 488 to reconstruct the full dendritic scaffold. This dual labeling enables both spine counting and normalization by dendritic length.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) CUBIC reagent A (urea, 10% v/v in 30% glycerol/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) CUBIC reagent A (urea, 20% v/v in 30% glycerol/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) CUBIC reagent A (urea, 30% v/v in 30% glycerol/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 100% CUBIC reagent A (urea, 100% v/v in 30% glycerol/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC reagent B (10% w/v iohexol in 30% glycerol/PBS, RI ≈ 1.42) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with CUBIC reagent C (20% w/v iohexol in 30% glycerol/PBS, RI ≈ 1.44) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with CUBIC reagent D (30% w/v iohexol in 30% glycerol/PBS, RI ≈ 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mounting in final CUBIC reagent D (30% w/v iohexol in 30% glycerol/PBS) for light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: As needed for imaging)

---

**Labeling Protocol Integration (Prior to Clearing):**

- **Endogenous GFP Expression:** Ensure transgenic mouse line expresses sparse GFP-labeled pyramidal neurons (e.g., Thy1-GFP-M or similar).
- **Immunostaining for MAP2:**
    - Fix tissue in 4% PFA/PBS for 24 h at 4 °C.
    - Permeabilize with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 h at RT.
    - Block with 5% normal goat serum in PBS for 1 h at RT.
    - Incubate with anti-MAP2 primary antibody (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution overnight at 4 °C.
    - Wash 3× with PBS for 15 min each.
    - Incubate with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000) in PBS for 2 h at RT.
    - Wash 3× with PBS for 15 min each.
    - Proceed to dehydration and clearing steps above.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a fast and effective lipid-clearing method suitable for fixed thick brain slices (e.g., 500 μm), with excellent compatibility with fluorescent proteins like GFP and synthetic dyes such as Alexa Fluor. It allows rapid dehydration and delipidation while preserving endogenous fluorescence and structural integrity of dendritic spines and neuronal architecture. The combination of GFP (for neuronal structure) and Phalloidin-AF568 (for F-actin in dendritic spines) provides dual labeling that enables high-resolution imaging of both dendritic skeletons and spine density.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM + 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining / Fluorescent Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (iDISCO-R; 40 vol% dibenzyl ether (DBE), 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Optional: Incubation with iDISCO-R overnight at 4 °C for improved clearing if time permits

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in iDISCO-R or DBE in a custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal imaging  
6.2 Store at 4 °C in the dark until imaging

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is compatible with fluorescent proteins like GFP and phalloidin-labeled F-actin. It avoids the harsh dehydration/delipidation steps of TDE or iDISCO+, which can cause tissue shrinkage and loss of fine dendritic spine structures. The protocol can be completed within 24 hours for 300–500 μm slices, making it ideal for rapid processing. Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 provides high-resolution labeling of dendritic spines, while GFP allows sparse labeling of neuronal somata and dendrites to aid in skeleton reconstruction.

---

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (10% (vol/vol) N-cyclohexyl-2-aminoethyl carbodiimide hydrochloride (CHAC), 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (10% (vol/vol) CHAC, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R3 (10% (vol/vol) CHAC, 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-Clear (50% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-Clear + 10% (vol/vol) RI-matching additive (e.g., 10% w/vol PEG400 in CUBIC-Clear) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount samples in CUBIC-Clear or 50% glycerol/PBS for light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

6 Optional Post-fixation Stabilization (if signal fading occurs)  
6.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in PBS for 1 hour at RT (only if necessary after clearing)  
6.2 Wash 3× with PBS for 10 min each

7 Fluorescent Labeling (before clearing)  
7.1 Permeabilize with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 15 min at RT  
7.2 Incubate with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated phalloidin (1:100 dilution in PBS) for 1 hour at RT in the dark  
7.3 Wash 3× with PBS for 10 min each  
7.4 Store in PBS until clearing begins

It uses a methanol-based dehydration and delipidation protocol that is compatible with lipid-soluble tracers used to label neural pathways. The method allows high-resolution 3D imaging using light-sheet microscopy, which is ideal for reconstructing cranial nerves, spinal nerves, and peripheral nerve branches in intact embryos.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Replace DMSO with 100% (vol/vol) methanol + 2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Repeat step 2.3 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in DBE (Diethyl Ether-Diiodomethane mixture) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)

5 RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE containing 0.1% (w/v) Pluronic F-127 (to reduce surface tension) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging

6 Fluorescent Labeling (Prior to Clearing)  
6.1 Incubation with 1 μM DiI in PBS (dissolved in ethanol; final ethanol concentration < 0.1%) for labeling peripheral nerves (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Wash 3× with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min each)  
6.3 Optional: If using transgenic mCherry reporter line, no additional staining is required. Otherwise, perform immunostaining with anti-mCherry antibody (1:500 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 + 2% BSA) followed by Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours for primary, 24 hours for secondary)  
6.4 Wash 3× with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min each)

7 Post-labeling Fixation  
7.1 Incubation with 4% (w/v) PFA in PBS for 2 hours at RT to stabilize fluorescent signals before proceeding to dehydration steps

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin + Alexa Fluor 488, tdTomato (endogenous)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole mouse embryos and provides excellent optical clearing while preserving fluorescent signals such as tdTomato and Alexa Fluor conjugates. It uses a methanol-based dehydration and delipidation protocol that is effective for lipid-rich neural tissues. β-III Tubulin (TuJ1) labeling with Alexa Fluor 488 allows visualization of early neuronal processes, while endogenous tdTomato can label more mature or lineage-specific neurons or axons. This combination enables dual-target imaging of both developing and established neural structures in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Replace DMSO/Triton solution with fresh 100% methanol (no detergent) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining (Optional if exogenous marker is needed)  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS + 5% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (e.g., TuJ1, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-Match solution (iDISCO-R1): 40% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE), 30% (w/v) sorbitol in PBS (RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-Match solution (iDISCO-R2): 40% (vol/vol) DBE, 50% (w/v) sorbitol in PBS (RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-Match solution (iDISCO-R3): 100% (vol/vol) DBE (RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24–48 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with 100% DBE (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: As needed for imaging)  
6.2 Use light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) or confocal microscopy for 3D imaging of tdTomato-labeled mature nerve bundles and Alexa Fluor 488-labeled early neurites

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a water-based clearing method that preserves endogenous and exogenous fluorescent signals well, making it ideal for whole-embryo imaging of complex neural structures such as cranial nerves, spinal nerves, and peripheral projections. It is compatible with long-term incubation and gentle washing steps, which are essential for preserving weak early-stage neurite signals. The use of GFP and tdTomato allows dual labeling of mature and immature neural elements without introducing new targets or fluorophores outside the provided list.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour, with gentle shaking)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (10% (vol/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) iohexol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.38) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (20% (vol/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) iohexol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R3 (30% (vol/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) iohexol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.42) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R4 (40% (vol/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) iohexol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.44) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R5 (50% (vol/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) iohexol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

5 Post-Clearing Washing and Stabilization  
5.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour, with gentle shaking)  
5.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour, with gentle shaking)  

6 Fluorescence Enhancement and Background Reduction  
6.1 Optional: Incubation with 0.1 mg/mL p-phenylenediamine (PPD) in PBS for fluorescence enhancement (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 0.1% Sudan Black B in 70% ethanol for background reduction (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Extensive washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour, with gentle shaking)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount sample in CUBIC-R5 for light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: As needed for imaging session)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synaptotagmin + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is a methanol-based clearing method specifically optimized for *Drosophila* tissues, including the brain and head with cuticle. It provides excellent optical transparency while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody labeling. The dual labeling strategy targets both presynaptic active zones (Bruchpilot) and synaptic vesicle-associated proteins (Synaptotagmin), enabling precise 3D mapping of synaptic structures and functional domains. This combination allows for high-resolution imaging of synaptic organization in intact brains using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS + 5% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies:  
   - Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) at 1:50 dilution  
   - Synaptotagmin at 1:100 dilution  
   (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min each)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies:  
   - Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG at 1:500  
   - Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG at 1:500  
   (Temperature: 4 °C, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min each)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with FlyClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Optional: Incubation with RI matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS) for additional clarity if needed (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in FlyClear or RI-matched mounting medium in a glass-bottom dish or custom chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: as required for imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx + Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for clearing mineralized and hard tissues such as bone, making it highly suitable for the P7 mouse calvarial suture region. It effectively removes lipids while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunostaining signals. The dual labeling strategy using Osx (Osterix) and Osteocalcin allows for the differentiation of osteoblast lineage stages: Osx marks early to pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts and osteocytes. This combination enables precise mapping of spatial distribution and differentiation dynamics in the suture and adjacent bone plates.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF in 100% ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining (Optional if not already labeled)  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Osx (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and Osteocalcin (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST), 3 × 15 min each (Temperature: RT, Time: 45 min total)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBST, 3 × 15 min each (Temperature: RT, Time: 45 min total)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Optional: Incubation with RI matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS) for additional optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount sample in RI-matched mounting medium or directly into imaging chamber filled with BoneClear (Temperature: RT, Time: As needed for imaging setup)  
6.2 Store at 4 ℃ in dark until imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy

**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone and cranial sutures, offering excellent optical clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunostaining signals. The labeling strategy uses Osx (Osterix) to mark early osteoblast progenitors and Osteocalcin to label mature osteoblasts and mineralized matrix, enabling the comparison of spatial distribution across different stages of osteogenic differentiation.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Repeat step 2.1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF/20% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) THF/40% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) THF/60% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) THF/80% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail:  
  – Anti-Osx (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
  – Anti-Osteocalcin (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)  
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (PBST) × 3 times (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail:  
  – Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 in blocking solution)  
  – Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500 in blocking solution)  
(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Wash with PBST × 3 times (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (Sigma-Aldrich or equivalent) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Optional: Replace BoneClear with fresh solution every 24 hours to enhance clearing efficiency

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mount sample in RI matching solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy imaging

**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx + mRFP, Cx43 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone and provides effective delipidation and refractive index matching while preserving endogenous fluorescence. It reduces background autofluorescence from mineralized tissue, which is critical for distinguishing early osteoblasts (e.g., Osx+) and mature osteoblasts (e.g., Cx43+). The labeling strategy uses Osx to mark pre-osteoblasts and Cx43 to label mature osteoblasts at the bone surface, enabling dual detection of different osteoblast lineages in a single sample. Alexa Fluor 594 conjugated secondary antibody ensures compatibility with BoneClear and minimizes spectral overlap with endogenous signals.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol/DCM (1:1 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Repeat step 2.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM/methanol (1:1 v/v) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in BoneClear reagent (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in BoneClear reagent (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in BoneClear reagent (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in BoneClear reagent (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) BoneClear reagent (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4.1 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 min)

  – Anti-Osx (1:200 dilution in blocking solution)

(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for clearing whole mouse bones while preserving endogenous and exogenous fluorescent signals. It is compatible with lipid removal in mineralized tissues and allows deep imaging of the bone marrow cavity using light-sheet or confocal microscopy. The labeling strategy targets TH to label sympathetic nerve fibers and CD31 to label endothelial cells, enabling co-localization analysis of nerves and vasculature within the intact bone marrow microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2 Lipid Removal  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol, Sigma-Aldrich B7639) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

5 RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent + 0.1% (wt/vol) Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-TH antibody (1:200 dilution) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-CD31 antibody (1:200 dilution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Final Clearing and Storage  
6.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Store sample in BoneClear reagent at 4 ℃ until imaging
